import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Map 'is_fraud' to descriptive labels for better legend readability
df['is_fraud_label'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'Not Fraud', 1: 'Fraud'})

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes for two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(12, 10), gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [1.5, 1]})

# Define custom colors for fraud vs. not fraud to make 'Fraud' stand out
colors = {'Not Fraud': 'steelblue', 'Fraud': 'firebrick'}

# Plot 1: Distribution of transaction amounts by type and fraud status
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', y='amount', hue='is_fraud_label', ax=axes[0], palette=colors, width=0.6)
axes[0].set_title('Transaction Amount Distribution by Type and Fraud Status', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if many types
axes[0].legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12, frameon=True)
axes[0].grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Plot 2: Count of transactions by hour of day and fraud status
sns.countplot(data=df, x='hour_of_day', hue='is_fraud_label', ax=axes[1], palette=colors)
axes[1].set_title('Transaction Counts by Hour of Day and Fraud Status', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[1].legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12, frameon=True)
axes[1].grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
# Ensure all hours are displayed if the range is small enough
if df['hour_of_day'].nunique() <= 24: # Adjust this threshold if needed
    axes[1].set_xticks(range(df['hour_of_day'].min(), df['hour_of_day'].max() + 1))

# Add a main title for the entire figure
fig.suptitle('Credit Card Fraud Analysis: Amount, Type, and Time Patterns', fontsize=18, weight='bold', y=1.02)

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles/labels
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rect to make space for the super title

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
